findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default rather than protected with SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS.

findings.issue_category: no public access block / ACL restriction
findings.description: The bucket has no ACL or public access block configuration set, leaving it reliant on AWS defaults and lacking explicit access controls, increasing risk of unintended public exposure.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket storing ledger export data, meaning sensitive financial data at rest is unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, leaving operational runbook content (which may include sensitive operational details) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; this is likely a misconfiguration that could either fail deployment or silently apply an unintended access grant that permits broader write access than intended for an audit log bucket.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all contained objects to be deleted without protection, removing a safeguard against accidental or malicious data loss; combined with no versioning this is a data integrity risk.

findings.issue_category: plaintext sensitive data upload without encryption enforcement
findings.description: An object containing what appears to be vendor roster data (potentially sensitive PII) is uploaded to a bucket with no encryption configuration and no explicit server_side_encryption parameter set on the object resource itself.

The ledger export bucket lacks versioning, meaning accidental overwrites or deletions of financial export data cannot be recovered, weakening integrity protections for sensitive data alongside the missing encryption.
